title: Venus and Adonis: Warning and Loss
subtitle: A warning, a hunt, and a flower

learningObjectives.text: What warning does Venus give Adonis?

warning.author: Ovid
warning.locator: Book X · Fable IX [X.519-707]; Book X · Fable IX [X.519-707], normalized characters 1723-2214
warning.excerpt: Forbear, youth, to be rash at my hazard, and attack not the wild beasts to which nature has granted arms, lest thy {thirst for} glory should cost me dear. Neither thy age, nor thy beauty, nor {other} things which have made an impression on Venus, make any impression on lions and bristly boars, and the eyes and the tempers of wild beasts. The fierce boars carry lightning[54] in their curving tusks; there is rage and fury unlimited in the tawny lions; and the {whole} race is odious to me.
warning.note: Verbatim translated verse from Ovid. Riley's arguments, synopses, notes, and explanations are separately indexed and are not quoted as primary verse.

flower.author: Ovid
flower.locator: Book X · Fable X [X.708-739]; Book X · Fable X [X.708-739], normalized characters 1254-1745
flower.excerpt: But thy blood shall be changed into a flower. Was it formerly allowed thee, Persephone, to change the limbs[65] of a female into fragrant mint; and shall the hero, the son of Cinyras, {if} changed, be a cause of displeasure against me?’ Having thus said, she sprinkles his blood with odoriferous nectar, which, touched by it, effervesces, just as the transparent bubbles are wont to rise in rainy weather. Nor was there a pause longer than a full hour, when a flower sprang up from the blood

narrativeBlocks.title: The goddess who fell for a hunter
narrativeBlocks.body: Scratched by Cupid's arrow, Venus falls hopelessly for the mortal hunter Adonis — and abandons heaven to tramp the hills at his side, a goddess acting the huntress.

narrativeBlocks.title: A lover's warning
narrativeBlocks.body: She warns him as she leaves: hunt only the timid creatures — never the fierce beasts that turn and fight. She even tells him Atalanta's story to make the lesson stick.

narrativeBlocks.title: The wound that kills
narrativeBlocks.body: Adonis ignores her: his hounds rouse a wild boar, his spear only wounds it — and the boar gores him to death in the groin. The hunter dies as hunters die.

narrativeBlocks.title: Blood into anemone
narrativeBlocks.body: Venus finds him dying and pours nectar on his blood: it swells and blooms into the anemone — the wind-flower, beautiful and as brief as the boy it remembers.

narrativeBlocks.title: Love and loss, one poem
narrativeBlocks.body: Ovid's Adonis is the pattern of the whole book: desire and grief are the same story, and a flower is the shape mourning takes.

quiz.prompt: What warning does Venus give Adonis?

choices.text: Hunt only timid game — never the fierce beasts that turn to fight

quiz.explanation: She warns him off the dangerous game — and he ignores it.

quiz.prompt: What does Adonis become at death?

choices.text: The anemone — the wind-flower sprung from his nectar-sprinkled blood

quiz.explanation: The brief anemone is his memorial — beauty as short-lived as he was.
